newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Deputy Magalhaes accepts job as Brazil chief whip.
newsitem.headline: Deputy Magalhaes accepts job as Brazil chief whip.

text.p: Brazilian deputy Luis Eduardo Magalhaes agreed Wednesday to serve as the government's chief whip in the lower house of Congress, a presidential spokesman said.

"Deputy Luis Eduardo talked with the leaders of political parties, made consultations and today came to tell the president that he accepts the invitation to be the government's leader in the Chamber of Deputies," spokesman Sergio Amaral said.
Amaral said Magalhaes told President Fernando Henrique Cardoso of his decision in the presence of Political Coordination Minister Luiz Carlos Santos to show the two men would work well together.
Newspapers have said the appointment of Magalhaes, considered one of the most influential members of Congress, was a snub to Santos and that the minister's authority had not been weakened.

Magalhaes secured approval of several important reform bills while president of the Chamber of Deputies between 1995 and February this year. He is also son of the government's most powerful ally, Senator Antonio Carlos Magalhaes.

Luis Eduardo's reputation as a heavyweight in Congress will be put to the test next week when the government hopes to resume voting on outstanding amendments to its civil service reform bill. That process has been on hold for nearly two months amid inter-party bickering and an alleged corruption scandal.
